title: Switchboard rings: First qualifying slip
summary: Graph breadth-first distances. Read the result list from left to right.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
links is a square table of 0s and 1s. Points are numbered from 0. A 1 at links[a][b] means a one-way path goes from point a to point b. A 0 means no path. k is a whole number. Use it as described in the steps below.

Step 1: Build the result list
A graph is a set of points joined by paths. Here, paths go in one direction. Start at point 0. For each point, find the fewest paths you must follow to reach it. Record these distances in point order: 0, 1, 2, and so on. The distance to point 0 is 0. Record -1 for a point you cannot reach. A graph with no points gives an empty result list.

Step 2: Return the answer
Read the result list from left to right. Return the first number that is at least k (greater than or equal to k). Return the number, not its position. If none matches, return -1.

Write your function
Complete switchboardRingsFirstQualifyingSlip(links, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.

Record these distances in point order: 0, 1, 2, and so on. The distance to point 0 is 0. Record -1 for a point you cannot reach. A graph with no points gives an empty result list. Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
The graph has at most 16 points. Its table has the same number of rows and columns. Link entries are 0 or 1; cost entries are 0 through 13.
Efficiency goal: time O(V^2); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length; V is the number of graph points. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
